card.name: Partsa
card.tagline: Guria's fast, festive dance of living towers
card.profile: Partsa is a fast-paced dance originating in Guria, characterized by rhythm, a festive mood and colorfulness (Wikipedia). It dazzles audiences with speed and gracefulness and with 'live towers' - dancers standing on others' shoulders. It is a famous version of the round dance perkhuli (the 'Gurian perkhuli'); the Sukhishvili ensemble performed Partsa on the stage of La Scala in Milan, reportedly the first and only time a folklore group performed on that stage (georgia.travel; Wikipedia).
card.insight: As a Gurian form of perkhuli, Partsa embodies the multi-level 'tower' tradition of western Georgian round dance; its La Scala performance was a landmark for Georgian folk dance on the world stage (georgia.travel).
card.image_significance: Gurian round dance with 'live towers'. A representative image shows upright carriage, sweeping arm lines and embroidered dress — Guria, Georgia.
